Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

punishment noun

also penalty, punishments, pay the penalty, suffer punishment, punishment for crimes, capital punishment, death penalty, suffer capital punishment, death sentence, condemn to death, receive the death sentence

classical

Cic. Off. 1.89
Cic. Leg. 3.11
Traupman 196, 258

poena, poenae f.

noun, first declension

punishment, penalty

To punish, poenā afficere; to be punished, poenās dare (see punish).

Other words

  • supplicium, suppliciī n. — punishment, especially a severe one; the death penalty

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Ter. And. 903; Traupman 194

    Properly a kneeling down; usually of the death penalty (Lewis & Short), though the father in Terence uses it of a small punishment.

  • animadversiō, animadversiōnis f. — punishment, official correction

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.88; Cic. Phil. 2.18

  • castīgātiō, castīgātiōnis f. — correction, punishment (of a child or a pupil)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.88; Quint. 1.3.14

  • supplicium capitis — capital punishment, the death penalty

    also used · classical · Traupman 286; Traupman 301

    Supplicium alone is often the death penalty; Traupman’s full phrase is supplicium capitis; “to suffer capital punishment”, suppliciō capitis afficī.

Examples

  • Prō peccātō magnō paulum supplicī satis est patrī.

    For a great wrong, a little punishment is enough for a father.Ter. And. 903

  • Cavendum est etiam nē major poena quam culpa sit

    One must also take care that the punishment is not greater than the faultCic. Off. 1.89

  • noxiae poena pār estō

    let the punishment fit the offenceCic. Leg. 3.11

  • poenās persolvere

    to pay the penaltyTraupman 196; cf. Cic. Phil. 11.29 (Lewis & Short s.v. persolvō)

  • poenās ferre

    to suffer punishmentTraupman 197

  • poena facinorum

    punishment for crimesTraupman 196

  • suppliciō capitis afficī

    to suffer capital punishmentTraupman 286

  • aliquem capitis damnāre

    to condemn someone to deathTraupman 301

  • capitis damnārī

    to receive the death sentenceTraupman 301

  • poenam dare

    to suffer punishmentTraupman 387

See also punish, crime, prison.
